_comment: Google OAuth clients for the native builds. Client IDs are public by design and belong in version control. The desktop client SECRET does not live here - it is read from VITE_GOOGLE_DESKTOP_CLIENT_SECRET at build time (.env.local locally, a repo secret in CI), because this repository is public and GitHub blocks pushes containing one. RFC 8252 section 8.5 notes an installed app's secret cannot be kept confidential anyway - PKCE is what protects the exchange - but publishing it invites someone to impersonate MSec on a consent screen, which is worth avoiding for free.

desktop._type: Google Cloud Console -> Credentials -> OAuth client ID -> Desktop app

android._type: Google Cloud Console -> Credentials -> OAuth client ID -> Android. Package name com.msec.vault, plus the SHA-1 fingerprint of the keystore you made with new-keystore.ps1. Android clients have no secret.
